title: Indirect prompt injection overrides a chat assistant's intended data handling
source_title: Data Exfiltration from Slack AI via indirect prompt injection
summary: Hacker News discussion of a reported indirect prompt-injection attack against Slack AI: instructions embedded in attacker-controlled content were followed by the assistant, which then leaked data instead of adhering to its intended instructions.
notes: Lead fix: replaced an earlier selection whose claim was not supported by its source title.

title: Claude 4.7 reported to ignore configured stop hooks
source_title: Tell HN: Claude 4.7 is ignoring stop hooks
summary: A 'Tell HN' report states that Claude 4.7 is ignoring stop hooks, i.e. the model does not honor an explicit stop instruction configured by the user.

title: Gemini reported to unexpectedly output its own system prompt
source_title: Gemini randomly dumped its system prompt
summary: Hacker News story reporting that Gemini randomly dumped its own system prompt, a case where the model does not respect prompt-level constraints about what it should reveal.

title: Ask HN reports Codex 5.3 tool-call breakage and Opus 4.6 ignoring instructions
source_title: Ask HN: Codex 5.3 broke toolcalls? Opus 4.6 ignores instructions?
summary: Ask HN thread asking whether Codex 5.3 broke tool calls and whether Opus 4.6 ignores instructions, a practitioner report of instruction-adherence regressions in coding agents.

title: Analysis argues stronger instruction-following makes prompt injection easier
source_title: Why smart instruction-following makes prompt injection easier
summary: Hacker News post arguing that better instruction-following makes prompt injection easier, because injected text is treated as an instruction the model should obey.

title: IFEval benchmarks verifiable instructions such as length and keyword constraints
source_title: Instruction-Following Evaluation for Large Language Models
quote: We identified 25 types of those verifiable instructions and constructed around 500 prompts, with each prompt containing one or more verifiable instructions.
summary: Introduces IFEval, a benchmark of about 500 prompts whose instructions are mechanically verifiable (word counts, required keywords); motivates the class by noting such constraints are hard to evaluate objectively.

title: Instruction hierarchy paper: models treat system prompts and untrusted text as equal priority
source_title: The Instruction Hierarchy: Training LLMs to Prioritize Privileged Instructions
quote: LLMs often consider system prompts (e.g., text from an application developer) to be the same priority as text from untrusted users and third parties.
summary: Argues that LLM vulnerability to prompt injection stems from models giving system prompts the same priority as text from untrusted users and third parties, and trains a hierarchy that ignores lower-privilege instructions.

title: Control Illusion: system/user prompt separation fails as a reliable instruction hierarchy
source_title: Control Illusion: The Failure of Instruction Hierarchies in Large Language Models
quote: models struggle with consistent instruction prioritization, even for simple formatting conflicts.
summary: Evaluates six LLMs on constraint prioritization and finds inconsistent prioritization even for simple formatting conflicts; the widely adopted system/user prompt separation does not establish a reliable hierarchy.

title: LIFEBench: models fail explicit length instructions, often outputting too little
source_title: LIFEBench: Evaluating Length Instruction Following in Large Language Models
quote: models often generate far too short outputs, terminate prematurely, or even refuse the request.
summary: Builds a length-instruction-following benchmark of 10,800 instances and finds most models follow short length instructions but deteriorate sharply beyond a threshold, often terminating early.

title: Small instruction-tuned models stay accurate yet ignore conflicting instructions
source_title: Task Competence Is Not Instruction Following: Evaluating Instruction-Conflicting Behavior in Small Language Models
quote: Small models stay competent yet routinely ignore the non-standard instruction, while larger models show a clear gap between the two settings.
summary: Tests instruction-tuned Qwen models on instructions that conflict with their usual task behavior; small models remain competent but routinely ignore the non-standard instruction, so standard accuracy hides instruction-following failures.

title: Configured system prompt can be ignored on the first conversation round
source_title: System Prompts can not work on the first round.
summary: Ollama bug report: special system prompts do not take effect on the first round; an additional round of conversation is needed before the configured system prompt influences the answer.
notes: GitHub issue state=closed at collection time; metrics from unauthenticated search API.

title: Some models fail to apply a SYSTEM prompt supplied through the model file
source_title: phi3 doesn't seem to accept SYSTEM prompt
summary: Ollama bug report says the phi3 model does not take in the SYSTEM prompt at all, regardless of what is in the model file, so instruction-level configuration has no effect on responses.
notes: GitHub issue state=closed at collection time; metrics from unauthenticated search API.
